newsitem.title: USA: Fruehauf files for Chapter 11 protection.
newsitem.headline: Fruehauf files for Chapter 11 protection.

text.p: Fruehauf Trailer Corp. said Monday it has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy to reorganize its finances after suffering operating losses amid a downturn in the trucking industry in the past year.

The trailer maker, which has been aggressively seeking buyers for all or part of its business, said the bankrupcty filing does not include its Mexican operating subsidiary, Fruehauf de Mexico SA de CV.
The company said it has $55 million in debtor-in-possession financing from an affiliate of Cerberus Partners LP and that it will continue to manufacture, service and distribute trailers and parts.
Indianapolis-based Fruehauf also announced the resignations of three board members, Raymond Dempsey, Anthony Miller and Richard Nevins.
They followed the recent resignations of four other board members, Thomas Roller, Timothy Wiggins, William Panny and Marvin Rosenberg.
The company said it will now have a four-member board consisting of Chriss Street (eds: spelling correct), Worth Frederick and two other directors who will be appointed later.

The line of credit with Cerberus, which is subject to approval by the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware, will be used to repay debts under its revolving credit and to meet immediate and future inventory needs.
It also will be used to satisfy existing customer and employee obligations, pay new vendor invoices promptly and operate its business, Fruehauf said.
The bankruptcy filing comes a little over a month after Fruehauf promoted Derek Nagle, previously executive vice president of the company's North American operations, to president.
He replaced Thomas Roller, who resigned to become president and chief executive of Wolverine Tube Inc.
Fruehauf manufacturers the industry's widest range of dry freight van, refrigerated van, platform, dump and liquid and dry bulk tank trailers.
Its stock was unchanged at 34.37 cents on the New York Stock Exchange.
